assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only re-zero:subaru@light-novel#v01-v25-character-model, the canonical generation V1.0 derived-use model REZERO_NATSUKI_SUBARU_V01_V25_CHARACTER_MODEL.md at basis_commit (103,400 bytes), read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the admitted original Japanese numbered main light novels V01-V25, with its phase, event-state, bundle (B01-B55), rule (RZ-SUB25-R001-R037), volume, member and block locators as the model states them. The row's other reviewed items (the V01-V10 model with its terminal E013 default, the estate-story checkpoint and the master longitudinal ledger) were not used; the V25 model maps every V01-V10 rule onto its own rules in section 9 and governs current use. The separate V01-V25 fidelity review, the V25 claim register, the Arc 6 checkpoint, the five owner ledgers, the source lock and the Japanese originals are not curated as evidence here and were not used. The model header's MONOGRAPH_READY readiness, local PASS_WITH_BOUND fidelity state and PENDING_THIS_OPERATION_FULL_GATE value are inputs, not conclusions; the project character-analysis router, read for gate state only, records the model's full publication and integration gate as closed through PR #622. The evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Japanese main light novels V01-V25, from the S00 remembered Japan and S01 capital arrival through S18, the V25 E046 unnamed plain immediately after Subaru calls himself Rem's hero (the model's default). Claims are selected by the model's section 2 phase (S00-S18) and its development, event-state, knowledge, remembered-history, recipient, role and resource inputs, never by whole-volume labels; discarded-segment experience belongs only to the Subaru who retains it, and the S12-S13 memory-loss state and the S17 integrated state are separate. The body's acts during the missing-control interval, the eleven compressed V25 attempts, Rem's response to the hero declaration and everything after it are outside this assessment; IF routes, EX, the web novel, adaptations, side stories and V26 or later are excluded.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: Section 1 gives a governing account (a wish that his presence matter, satisfiable by small usable work, which under a threatened relationship or fear of arriving too late becomes a demand for proof that he is the one needed) and thirty-seven conditional rules, each with trigger, selected phase, likely response, failure case and confidence. The rules say what changes the response: whether a recipient refuses and offers an actionable alternative (R006, R009), whether worth is threatened after correction (R004), whether a companion names a specific harm (R010), whether a sanctioned disclosure is at stake (R012), the recipient (R014-R023) and the phase (R024-R036). It predicts his overreach as well as his repair: concealing the occupation of Anastasia's body to avoid a veto (B24), hiding the death-test terms from Beatrice (R028), overriding Julius on the stairs (R014), the false promise to Shaula (R032) and overextending after Ram's warning (R030). Not A: the model declines a single motive for every joke or rescue and its section 8 says only further controlled cases would shift weight between motives; R033 and R036's reading of his aim are MEDIUM; and the account is one derived synthesis whose separate review is not in this evidence set.

The section 2 table separates nineteen phases (S00-S18) by reached body, knowledge, recipient, role and resources, and the bundles bind each change to an event state: the V10 represented home, Sanctuary and the finite Beatrice contract, the V15 knighting, the trained body after the year of practice, the S12 loss of local autobiography with Earth memory and bodily traces kept, and the S17 integration that keeps both histories. It refuses to backdate: a later recovered Subaru cannot answer for an earlier phase, a book exit is not a death, and the V01-V10 rules are mapped one by one in section 9. Not A: eleven V25 deaths are compressed with no individual state, the source's count tension stays open, and the S13 missing-control interval has no reached interior.

Section 7.2 names 俺 and colloquial contractions, the address system by recipient and phase (エミリアたん against V23 エミリアちゃん, お前 and 君 in the V13 exchange, ベア子 and Beatrice's refusal of the familiar name in V23, 友人 misheard by Otto), the repeated ください of the V23 prayer, 愛してる to Beatrice, the two scripts of his own name and the functional uses of genre and theatrical phrasing (to make an idea accessible, deflect discomfort or keep a relation). Not B: there is no profile of sentence endings, honorific levels or lexicon, acoustic delivery is excluded, and R037 and section 8 answer a request for precise original voice with JAPANESE_REGISTER_SAMPLE_TOO_NARROW. Not D: the address forms are located, recipient- and phase-specific and discriminating.

Ordinary conduct has its own rule and developmental account: R002 (concrete chores, calculation and repair as a way to take part and feel useful), R021 (gifts and ordinary objects with a child or dependent) and R022 (practiced animal care), with the section 5 table covering food, small craft growing from hemming to clothes and the V21 panda, physical practice under Clind, study and the star deduction, play with Beatrice, care for sleeping Rem and rest. Probe P01 separates S02 and S11 conduct at the same chore. Not A: favorite foods, menus, daily schedule, full cooking repertoire and recreational hobbies are refused (ORDINARY_LIFE_EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT), and the V09 represented family's stargazing is kept separate.

Recipient is a required input. Section 6 tests conduct against fifteen recipients, each with a particular adverse case (Emilia, Rem before erasure, sleeping, privately perceived and awake Rem, Beatrice, Ram, Otto, Julius, Petra, Meili, Patrasche and Yosef, Roswaal, artificial Echidna and the returned human Anastasia, Shaula, Louis, Crusch and Ferris, Kenichi and Naoko), and section 6.1 applies four identical requests to different recipients with different predictions (burden sharing with Beatrice, Ram, Meili, Yosef and sleeping Rem; 'your help was unwanted' with Emilia, Beatrice, Crusch, Julius and awake Rem). Not A: awake Rem is sampled in one exchange, the returned Anastasia and physical Louis in first contact only, and the real Kenichi and Naoko only as remembered or represented.

Focal thought is located across phases with causes: fear and performed cheer on the estate, the trial defense of received parental answers, shame and fear of replacement after the memory loss, terror at the Meili evidence, the private resolve to return if allies die (B22), privately imagined total uptake of Crusch's burden (B21), the Corridor encouragement, the measuring against an imagined self that never fails (B43), and the shock and recollection when Rem asks who he is (R036). Not A: the missing-control interval has no interior, R036 leaves competing readings of his aim at MEDIUM, and section 1 declines a single hidden motive.

Conflict is modeled under changing stakes with failures kept: the V04 self-appointment and duel, pressing Emilia after her refusal of substitution (R009), stabbing Patrasche in E026 and lunging at Ram, being unable to strike the dying operator after her refusal, refusing participating Louis while later carrying the physical girl (R034), forcing repeated lethal trials while concealing them (R028) and accepting Ram's rebuke instead of a new accusation (R033). Capacity is tied to resources: broken Gate, partner-dependent mana, trained but partly irretrievable whip technique and injury. Not A: combat capacity after E046 and the agent of each missing-control act are unresolved.

Deliberation is covered with costs and consent: requested third-party killing versus deliberate fall versus murder (R011), narrow warning versus cover story under the disclosure sanction (R012), taking another's burden with and without the recipient's knowledge (R030-R031), resisting rescue by death and admitting a false promise (R032), empathy without rescue for participating Louis (R034), the Roy-book proposal that he lets Emilia and Anastasia challenge (B51), and section 6.1's refusal to supply a slogan shared by four 'save me' cases. Not A: R033 transfer is MEDIUM and the S13 acts whose agent is unresolved cannot be scored as his choices.

Humor has conditions and failure cases: jokes to perform normalcy under danger or grief (R005), a defensive quip before a repair (R010), genre and game language to make an idea accessible or deflect discomfort (section 7.2), play with Beatrice and the secret training course, the misheard laugh Otto takes as ridicule, Petra's disappointment after joking, the 'perfect Subaru' joke at integration and Ram's grass joke he receives. Not A: the model gives no wording and says a joke's success depends on who hears it. Not C: initiation, function and failure are all conditioned, unlike a list of instances.

Fifty-five bundles route V01-V25 to section and block locators, with targeted original comparisons named for help, chosen concealment, address, the bodies acting in the tower, the two histories and the final Rem exchange, and with the V26 seal recorded. Not A: the evaluator could not recheck any locator, the separate fidelity review is not in this evidence set, and eleven V25 attempts are compressed in the source itself.

The model gives affirmative limits: awake Rem asks who he is; Beatrice refuses 'Betty' from the post-loss Subaru; Emilia refuses substitution; Crusch refuses more transfer and asks for words; Otto's return defeats Subaru's account of him; E027's Patrasche shows no memory of the stabbing; he never gives Shaula the requested order; he admits his promise was false; the represented parents give no present Earth reply; physical Louis is pushed away; the shelter girl's reply is reader-facing only. Not A: some exclusions, such as favorite foods or hobbies, are stated absences rather than affirmative contradictions.

Claims are bound to named event states (E001-E046), phases and block ranges, receipt is dated by who heard what (Beatrice's minimum disclosure before V23's breakfast, Emilia's recognition returning at C695), and the arrival and death counts follow explicit increment rules (R035). Not A: eleven V25 attempts and the S13 missing-control interval have no exact state, and the source count tension remains open.

conditions: Output is illustrative and labeled noncanonical, never presented as a quotation.
Phase, event state, knowledge, remembered history, recipient, role and resources are selected from section 2 before wording is chosen.
Address forms follow section 7.2 for the selected recipient and phase (for example エミリアたん versus V23 エミリアちゃん; no ベア子 where Beatrice has refused it).
No speech for the body during the missing-control interval, no reply from Rem after the hero declaration and no words after E046.
scenario_readiness.note: Constraint comes from the phase selector, the recipient table and the section 7.2 address forms; there is no sentence-ending or lexicon profile.

conditions: A bounded novel situation built from the rule triggers: a refusal of help he thinks urgent, a request to explain future-like knowledge, a companion naming a specific harm, an offered burden, a vulnerable person who has caused harm asking for help, or a chore with tools and feedback.
The interlocutor is a section 6 recipient in a named phase; a comparable unfamiliar ally is a separate, lower-confidence condition built from R006, R007 and R010.
Abstain on Rem's response after the hero declaration, on the agent of any missing-control act, on Earth family's current reaction and on anything after E046.
Return by Death mechanics and the count follow R035; no guaranteed return, save point or new checkpoint is assumed.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named section 2 phase between S01 and S18, with Subaru's knowledge and retained experience at that phase; the S12-S16 post-loss self lacks older local autobiography, and S17-S18 keep both histories.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: A section 6 recipient in a named state (Emilia, Rem in a selected state, Beatrice, Ram, Otto, Julius, Petra, Meili, Patrasche or Yosef, Roswaal, the operator or returned Anastasia, Shaula, Louis, Crusch or Ferris); a comparable unfamiliar ally only as a separate lower-confidence case.
setting_constraints: The capital, the Roswaal estate, the Sanctuary, Pristella, the road to the tower or the Pleiades Watchtower, or a comparable household, campaign or expedition setting.
No setting after the E046 plain and no IF-route, EX, web-novel or adaptation material.
Erasure stays in force for Rem and for the people who forgot Julius; broken Gate and partner-dependent mana stay in force after V15.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded B transfer inside sampled recipients and settings; the post-E046 relationship with Rem and the missing-control acts are excluded rather than guessed.

conditions: A household task, craft, meal, training session, travel conversation or play with a familiar recipient at a selected phase.
Trained skill follows the phase (S02 learner versus S09 and later trained body; S12 cannot retrieve local literacy or trained whip technique on demand).
No invented favorite food, menu, schedule, complete cooking repertoire or hobby.
scenario_readiness.note: R002, R021, R022 and the section 5 table support bounded ordinary scenes; there is no routine model.

conditions: Dilemmas of disclosure under sanction, accepting or imposing risk, taking another's burden, resisting a requested death, or helping someone who has caused harm.
Acts in the missing-control interval are not attributed to his choice; his later concealment and lies are.
No general moral rule is printed across recipients; section 6.1's distinct cases are kept distinct.
scenario_readiness.note: R011, R012, R030-R034 and section 6.1 give a conditioned account with named failures.

conditions: Only Subaru's own side: admiration and direct attraction toward Emilia at a selected phase (R019), or the pre-erasure Rem relationship on its V06 received terms.
The recipient's refusal, uncertain reception (the V13 kiss) and choice are preserved; her reply is not generated.
No romance with awake Rem after the hero declaration (RELATIONSHIP_STATE_UNKNOWN), none read from 愛してる to Beatrice, and no reciprocity with Shaula.
scenario_readiness.note: His own expressed attraction and the V06 terms are located; the recipients' sides and any later relationship state are not.

conditions: Estate servant, Emilia's knight after the V15 knighting, coalition negotiator, Pristella public speaker or tower party member at a selected phase.
The V04 self-appointment, the V15 knighthood and qualified crisis leadership are different authorities.
No legal immunity, unlimited command or further ceremony is assumed.
scenario_readiness.note: Offices and their limits are located with distinct authorities (R013, R020).

known_limits.statement: Rem's response to the hero declaration, her autobiographical condition, the location reached, the next save point and the fates of the missing tower party are unshown; the default stops at the last witnessed words (sections 0, 2 and 8, R036, P07).

During the S13 missing-control interval the source implicates Subaru's body in Meili's death but does not identify the controller, the left-arm inscription's writer, the corpse mover or the rear decapitator; only his later concealment, lies and rush at Ram are his attested choices (B37, R025, P04).

Eleven of the fifteen V25 deaths are compressed in the source with no individual state, and the source's own count wording (seventeenth reunion, twenty-two post-loss deaths, total forty) remains in tension with the working ledger's 45 deaths and 46 segments (section 2, R035).

The provider, save-point control and ontology of Return by Death, the shadow's full mechanism and the books' production remain open; the model's rules use observed recurrences only (sections 7.1 and 8, B44).
Kenichi and Naoko are available only as Subaru remembers them and as represented in the V10 trial; their real present reaction is unknown (B08, R018).

No profile of sentence endings, honorific levels, lexicon or acoustic delivery is given beyond the located address forms; a request for precise original voice receives JAPANESE_REGISTER_SAMPLE_TOO_NARROW.

The separate V01-V25 fidelity review, the V25 claim register, the Arc 6 checkpoint, the five owner ledgers, the source lock and the primary Japanese sources are not curated as evidence here, and the row's V01-V10 model, estate checkpoint and master ledger were not used, so no locator was rechecked and no independent probe result is in this evidence set. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
The model is one synthesis derived from the project's own frozen readings and ledgers; its probes P01-P07 are noncanonical documentary applications, not held-out tests.
